evidence.title: Civilian Unemployment Rate
evidence.summary: The snapshotted target change was 0.2 percentage points; it resolved to 'above recent range'.

evidence.title: The Employment Situation - June 2024
evidence.summary: The unemployment rate in June 2024 was 4.1 percent, which is higher than the 3.6 percent from a year earlier. This directly states the unemployment rate for the target period.

evidence.title: Jobs report June 2024:
evidence.summary: The unemployment rate unexpectedly climbed to 4.1%, tied for the highest level since October 2021. This confirms the June 2024 unemployment rate and highlights its increase.

evidence.title: June 2024 U.S. Job Update
evidence.summary: The unemployment rate increased 10 bps from May to June, registering at 4.1%, the highest level since November 2021. This explicitly states the increase in basis points (0.1 percentage points) and the resulting rate.

evidence.title: June US Jobs Report: 206,000 Rise In Payrolls, but Revisions Show Slower Growth | Morningstar
evidence.summary: The unemployment rate, which had been forecast to stay at 4.0% from May to June, instead ticked to 4.1%. This confirms the June unemployment rate and the change from the previous month's expectation.

evidence.title: Employment Report: 206K Jobs Added in April, More Than Expected
evidence.summary: The latest unemployment rate is at 4.054% (to three decimal places), its level since November 2021. This provides the precise unemployment rate for June 2024, which rounds to 4.1%.

evidence.title: Employment up 206,000 over the month in June 2024 : The Economics Daily : U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
evidence.summary: This source, from the BLS, confirms the overall employment increase in June 2024, which is a related but not direct measure of the unemployment rate change. It provides context for the labor market conditions.

evidence.title: June jobs report preview: Beveridge curve implies a balanced labor market as hiring cools
evidence.summary: This preview expected the unemployment rate to remain unchanged at 4%. This provides a forecast that was contradicted by the actual outcome, highlighting the unexpected nature of the increase.

evidence.title: ADP National Employment Report: Private Sector Employment Increased by 150,000 Jobs in June; Annual Pay was Up 4.9% - Jul 3, 2024
evidence.summary: This report indicates an increase in private sector employment for June. While not directly the unemployment rate, it provides a related labor market indicator that might suggest a different trend than the unemployment rate increase.
